title: Live-in relationships - what legal protection actually exists
p1:
Many people believe a live-in relationship means having no legal rights at all. The reality is more complicated — and often surprising.

A couple living together may not have the same legal status as a married couple, but that does not mean the law completely ignores their relationship.
p2:
One common misconception is that partners in a live-in relationship can never seek protection. In many cases, the law can recognize certain rights, especially where there is evidence of a genuine, long-term relationship.

For example, protections related to domestic violence, financial support in certain situations, and the rights of children born from such relationships may exist depending on the facts and applicable law.
p3:
The key idea is this: living together does not automatically create the same rights as marriage, but it also does not leave people without any legal options. Documents, shared responsibilities, and the nature of the relationship can matter when legal questions arise.

The practical takeaway: know your rights before you need them.
